page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor platform. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz, the instance features 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. It is provisioned with 8.0 GB of RAM, offering a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio equal to 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance incorporates a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth capacity and includes zero bundled local storage, requiring external block storage for persistent data requirements. Supported hardware instruction extensions include AVX-512, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA.

Performance benchmark testing positions the ecs.c5.xlarge in the lower performance brackets relative to broader market options. The processor recorded a multi-core stress-ng score of 2,934.50 and a PassMark CPU score of 3,628.64. Memory throughput tests showed uncached large-block read speeds of 20.58 GB/sec and write speeds of 18.68 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom 10% to 25% categories. Key-value store benchmarks measured 2.86 million operations per second for Redis SET requests, while static web serving throughput achieved 3.36 GB/sec.

Given its 1:2 memory configuration and entry-tier CPU benchmark positioning, the instance is structured for entry-level compute workloads rather than memory-dense or high-throughput analytics. The absence of local disk drives shifts storage dependencies entirely to network volumes. Primary workload fits include basic web serving, modest key-value caching, low-volume background batch jobs, and small-scale software compilation.
